title: Osaka transformed from dangerous floater to title threat at Indian Wells 2018, pummelling a succession of former World No.1s and Slam champions to storm to her maiden trophy.
Daniela Hantuchova's first two WTA titles both came at Indian Wells as she claimed her second trophy five years after the first, defeating Svetlana Kuznetsova 6-3, 6-4 in the 2007 final.

In the final, Halep got off to a lightning start and didn't look back, never dropping serve as she closed Cibulkova out 6-2, 6-4 to capture the second Premier Mandatory trophy of her career following Indian Wells 2015.

Kim Clijsters took her second Miami trophy in 2010, dethroning Victoria Azarenka 6-4, 6-0 in round four, edging Justine Henin 6-2, 6-7(3), 7-6(6) in the SFs and capturing her third post-maternity title 6-2, 6-1 over Venus Williams in the final (Getty)

2014 saw Serena Williams successfully defend five titles, the most in any season of her career, including a victory over Sara Errani to win a third Rome trophy (Getty)
In 2007, Henin hoisted the trophy on the clay courts of Warsaw before taking home her fourth Roland Garros title.
Camila Osorio successfully defended her Bogota title in 2025, lifting the trophy for the third time overall. Her home tournament accounts for all three of Osorio's WTA titles so far.
Diyas returned to the final and took the trophy in 2017, besting home favorite Miyu Kato 6-2, 7-5 (Getty)

Dinara Safina continued to sweep through the 2009 clay season, adding the Madrid trophy to her Rome title with a 6-2, 6-4 win over Caroline Wozniacki in the final - the only time the pair ever faced off.
Kim Clijsters took home the trophy in an all-Belgian affair in 2010, beating Justine Henin 6-3, 4-6, 7-6 (Getty)
Serena Williams: 2009 Doha - Serena defeated Venus in the WTA Finals’ only all-Williams final to take home the 2009 trophy. (Getty Images)
World No.1 Iga Swiatek became the first Polish player ever to win a WTA title on home soil at Warsaw 2023. The trophy was Swiatek's 15th overall.
Two weeks after winning her first title on home soil, Coco Gauff lifted her second at Cincinnati 2023 -- the first WTA 1000 trophy of the 19-year-old's career.
In 2000, Mary Pierce claimed a title on the green clay of Hilton Head before she hoisted the trophy on home soil at Roland Garros.
Marie Bouzkova kept the Prague trophy in Czech hands after winning her maiden title in 2022, becoming the fifth home champion in the previous eight editions of the tournament.
Cornet (pictured here with her 2016 Hobart trophy) won six singles titles and three doubles titles on the Hologic WTA Tour. She also captured the Junior Roland Garros title on home soil in 2007.
Both of Zhang Shuai's WTA titles have come in Guangzhou, with the Chinese player picking up her second trophy there in 2018 after beating Aleksandra Krunic in the final.
The trophy was back in Russian hands in 2007 as they defeated Italy in the final. Svetlana Kuznetsova won two singles ties as the home side swept their opponents 4-0.
Ann Li rose 50 places, from No.97 to No.47. In 2021, the American won her first WTA singles title in Tenerife and also made the final of the Grampians Trophy in Melbourne.
In her third Nottingham final, Johanna Konta lifted the trophy for the first time in 2021, becoming the first British woman to win a title on home soil since Sue Barker at Brighton 1981.
In 2010, Vania King and Yaroslava Shvedova became the first couple to come from a set down in the final to win the trophy since the Williams sisters in 1999. They beat Huber and Nadia Petrova.

Osaka ended 2019 in hot form, picking up a first title on home soil in Osaka and following that with the Beijing trophy - ultimately putting together a 14-match winning streak, the longest of her career to date.

Garbiñe Muguruza toppled World No.1 Serena Williams in the 2016 Roland Garros final for the Spaniard's first Grand Slam title. The very next year, Muguruza notched her second major trophy at Wimbledon and rose to World No.1.
Li Na got her hands on the trophy at last in 2010 when she beat Maria Sharapova 7-5, 6-1 in the final; it was the only one of the Chinese two-time Slam champion's titles to come on grass (Getty)

When Kvitova defeated Elina Svitolina 6-4, 6-2 to finish 2016 with victory at the Zhuhai Elite Trophy, it was the culmination of a superb fall swing - but a month later, tragedy struck when the Czech suffered a knife attack at home in Prostejov (Getty)

After receiving the walkover from Williams, Kvitova took the first set from Halep in their semifinal clash. The 2011 champion then dropped the last two sets to Halep -- but Kvitova was just one year away from hoisting the Madrid trophy for a second time.

A marathon final saw Petra Kvitova triumph over Kiki Bertens 7-6(6), 4-6, 6-3 after two hours and 52 minutes to seal her fourth title of 2018, and 24th overall - as well as becoming the first player to lift the Madrid trophy three times.
Serena had her name etched on the trophy once more in 2012 as she scored a 6-3, 6-4 victory over rival Maria Sharapova. (Getty)
Caroline Wozniacki routed Maria Sharapova 6-1, 6-2 in the semifinals and battled past Marion Bartoli 6-1, 2-6, 6-3 in the final to win her 14th career trophy in 2011.

Svitolina was at her best in routing Halep 6-1, 6-1 in the semifinals of Toronto 2017 en route to lifting her fifth trophy of the year (Getty)

Justine Henin won the 40th of her 43 career titles here in 2008, beating Svetlana Kuznetsova 4-6, 6-2, 6-4 in the final - the penultimate trophy of the Belgian's first career (Getty)

Hometown heroine Timea Babos took the trophy at the inaugural Hungarian Ladies Open indoor event in 2017, beating Julia Goerges in the semifinals and Lucie Safarova 6-7(4), 6-4, 6-3 in the final (Getty)

Kateryna Bondarenko won her maiden title in 2009, beating Yanina Wickmayer 7-6(7), 3-6, 7-6(4) in the first Birmingham final to be decided be a final set tiebreak; Bondarenko would have to wait nine years for her second trophy, in Tashkent 2017 (Getty)

Venus Williams has won six titles since turning 32: Luxembourg 2012, Dubai 2014, Auckland, Wuhan and the Zhuhai Elite Trophy in 2015, and the former World No.1's most recent trophy, Kaohsiung 2016, captured at the age of 35 years and seven months.

Fresh off defending her Australian Open title, Azarenka would eventually snap Williams's streak of wins in the 2013 Doha final, saving a set point in the first set to claim her 16th trophy 7-6(6), 2-6, 6-3.

Venus delivered the only bagel set of their rivalry in the round robin stages of the 2008 Doha WTA Finals, triumphing 5-7, 6-1, 6-0 over Serena in the round-robin stages and going on to lift her first trophy at the season-ending championships.
2018 Indian Wells champion Naomi Osaka kept things casual as she waited for her tiebreak against Amanda Anisimova.

2006 Indian Wells champion Maria Sharapova made it to the Miami final when Tatiana Golovin retired in their semifinal, but fell to Svetlana Kuznetsova 6-4, 6-3 in the final (Getty)
In 2002, shock Indian Wells champion Daniela Hantuchova couldn't sustain her momentum in Miami, falling 4-6, 6-4, 6-2 to World No.75 Cara Black in her second-round opener (Getty)
Elena Vesnina became just the second Indian Wells champion to lose their Miami opener in 2017, falling 3-6, 6-4, 7-5 to No.594-ranked wildcard Ajla Tomljanovic in the second round (Getty)

No.286-ranked Liv Hovde, the 2022 Wimbledon junior champion, notched the second and third Top 100 wins of her career over Aliaksandra Sasnovich and Harriet Dart to qualify for Indian Wells. The 18-year-old American fell to Lesia Tsurenko in Round 1.

Australian Open winner Kenin's loss to Azarenka was just the second time in the Open Era that a reigning Grand Slam champion had been double bagelled, following Maria Sharapova's loss to Lindsay Davenport at Indian Wells 2005.

Shock 2018 Indian Wells champion Naomi Osaka was still unseeded in Miami, and scored a first-round win over childhood idol Serena Williams before falling 6-4, 6-2 to Elina Svitolina in the second round (Getty)

Late-blooming Flavia Pennetta won the two biggest titles of her career after turning 32 - Indian Wells 2014 and the 2015 US Open, where she became the oldest first-time Grand Slam champion ever at the age of 33.

2008 Indian Wells champion Ana Ivanovic fell 6-4, 6-2 to Lindsay Davenport, who was returning from maternity leave and ranked World No.33, in the third round of Miami - one of two Top 5 wins the American gained in her comeback (Getty)

Defending champion Serena Williams has reached two finals this year, and the nine-time Miami Open champion hopes familiar ground will lead her to her first 2016 title.
In 2007, Raymond and Stosur joined forces to tremendous effect once more as they again did the Double. Cara Black and Liezel Huber were only beaten on a champions tiebreak in the final of Miami.
Danielle Collins won her first WTA 1000 title at Miami 2024 in her home state, becoming the first American champion of the tournament since Sloane Stephens in 2018.

University of Miami alumna, 2019 Wimbledon junior finalist and 2024 NCAA singles champion Alexa Noel received a US Open wild card. The 21-year-old No.784-ranked American fell to Sara Sorribes Tormo in Round 1.
A record eighth Miami crown for Serena Williams followed in 2015, as the two-time defending champion swept past Carla Suárez Navarro in the final, 6–2, 6–0.

Serena Williams's first Miami title in 2002 was won without the loss of a set: the American routed 1997-2001 champions Martina Hingis 6-4, 6-0 and Venus Williams 6-2, 6-2 before overcoming Jennifer Capriati 7-5, 7-6(4) in the final (Getty)
Victoria Azarenka became a two-time Miami champion in 2011, defeating Maria Sharapova, 6-1, 6-4, in the final. Azarenka won the event two years prior, defeating Serena Williams in the 2009 final.

15-year old Roland Garros girls' champion Cori Gauff received a Miami wildcard - and became the youngest player since Madison Keys in 2009 to win a WTA main draw match, beating Catherine McNally in the first round (Jimmie48/WTA)

In its six editions, Prague has seen three home champions, with Petra Kvitova the most recent in 2018 after her final defeat of Mihaela Buzarnescu.
Having had no home champions since 1998, Japan got two in as many weeks in September 2019, with Naomi Osaka picking up her first home title in Osaka, the city of her birth, without dropping a set.
Mary Pierce ended France's 33-year wait for a home champion with her victory in Paris in 2000.
2018 champion Karolina Pliskova is on the comeback trail from a wrist fracture, and devoted some time to honing her renowned serve.
Barbora Krejcikova continued her 2022 autumn resurgence by becoming the first home champion in Ostrava - the Czech's second title in her own country.

Future Roland Garros champion Francesca Schiavone reached her first major quarterfinal in 2001 at the age of 20, ranked World No.51 and fresh off her first Rome quarterfinal, via a third-round upset of No.10 seed Amanda Coetzer.
Having retired from singles in 2022, former US Open champion Samantha Stosur played her final doubles match on home soil at the Australian Open alongside Alizé Cornet.
World No.123 Viktorija Golubic was a champion on home soil in 2016, when she defeated Kiki Bertens to win the Gstaad title.
The inaugural Baltic Open in Jurmala, Latvia in 2019 ended with a home champion as Anastasija Sevastova defeated Katarzyna Kawa in the final.
Coco Gauff, 19, became the third American champion on home soil this decade when she won her first WTA 500 title, and fourth overall, at Washington 2023.

Victoria Azarenka overturned a double-break final-set deficit to score her third Top 10 win of 2019 in the second round of Rome, saving one match point down 2-5 to oust defending champion Elina Svitolina 4-6, 6-1, 7-5 (Jimmie48/WTA)
Barbora Krejcikova became the sixth home champion in Prague since the inaugural 1992 edition after winning the tournament's third all-Czech final over Tereza Martincova in 2021.
Alizé Cornet, the 2013 Strasbourg champion and 2012 runner-up, found her feet on home soil once again with a straight-sets first-round defeat of Polona Hercog.

No.1 seed and 2015 Dubai champion Simona Halep thrilled her Romanian supporters in the U.A.E. with a come-from-behind quarterfinal victory over No.7 seed Aryna Sabalenka.

title: Australian Open champion and World No.1 Amélie Mauresmo was beaten in the fourth round of her home major in 2006, losing in three sets to Czech teenager Nicole Vaidisova.

The inaugural edition of Lexington in 2020 featured three American semifinalists - and it was Jennifer Brady who eventually became a champion on home soil, defeating Jil Teichmann to claim her maiden title.
Caroline Garcia defeated Mirjana Lucic-Baroni in the 2016 Strasbourg final to pick up her second career title and first at home - also becoming the third French champion in the tournament's history.
The two-time Grand Slam champion was playing in Prague for the first time, having last played a clay court International tournament at home in Bucharest, where she also won in 2016.

Nottingham 2023 saw Katie Boulter win her first career title, defeating Jodie Burrage in the first all-British WTA final since San Francisco 1977. Andy Murray, champion in the ATP Challenger event held alongside, completed the home singles sweep.

Former World No.30 Misaki Doi, the 2015 Luxembourg champion, ended her career with a run to the second round on home soil in Tokyo. Former junior peer Kurumi Nara presented flowers to Doi after her loss to Maria Sakkari.
Hobart's most recent home champion was Jarmila Wolfe, who took her second career title in 2011 without dropping a set all week, beating Bethanie Mattek-Sands 6-4, 6-3 in the final (Getty)

Ranked World No.35, a 20-year-old Garbiñe Muguruza rode her second-round upset of No.1 seed Serena Williams all the way to her maiden Grand Slam quarterfinal in 2014 - two years before becoming Roland Garros champion.

[5] Liudmila Samsonova d. Barbora Krejcikova 6-2, 6-7(5), 6-4, Strasbourg R1 (3:00). Samsonova led 5-2 in the second set and held her first match point at 5-4, but had to come from 3-1 down in the decider to defeat the 2021 champion.

Angelique Kerber rose to No.1 after winning her second Slam title at the US Open in 2016, a year when she was also Australian Open champion and finalist at Wimbledon, the Olympic Games and the WTA Finals, and has notched up 34 weeks at the summit (Getty)
Back on home soil, Williams claimed the 2002 US Open, once again besting her sister Venus in the championship match. Williams did not drop a set en route to her second US Open crown.
No player has won more frequently on the grass since 2000 than Serena Williams. All of her eight titles have come at Wimbledon, seven at The Championships and the other at the 2012 Olympics.

Playing some of her best tennis in several years, Venus followed that up with success at the 2008 WTA Tour Championships. She defeated four of the Top 5 to win the title for the first time, doing so unbeaten.

Among her other highlights include the 2011 WTA Finals championship, eight WTA 1000 titles (including three in Madrid), and a finalist showing at the 2019 Australian Open.

Victoria Jimenez Kasintseva, 15, became the first ever Andorran to play in a WTA main draw when she received a wildcard for Madrid. The 2020 Australian Open junior champion, ranked World No.901, fell to Kiki Bertens in round one.

At the 2013 Mutua Madrid Open, the 16 seeds were the Top 16 players in the world, led by reigning champion and World No.1 Serena Williams. The American started her title defense with a first-round win over Yulia Putintseva.
2008 champion Maria Sharapova had the day's most emphatic win, shutting qualifier Harriet Dart out 6-0, 6-0 (Getty)

Fresh off the Prague title, No.10 seed Petra Kvitova, previously a Madrid champion in 2011 and 2015, dropped just one set - to Anett Kontaveit in the third round - en route to the last four, routing Daria Kasatkina 6-4, 6-0 in the quarterfinals.

Australian Open champion Victoria Azarenka played three thrillers as No.1 seed in 2012, overcoming defending champion Samantha Stosur and Maria Sharapova before coming runner-up to Serena Williams by a 6-2, 2-6, 7-5 scoreline.

No.4 seed Venus Williams came into Madrid with a 21-3 record in 2010, and racked up quality wins on her way to the last four: Vera Zvonareva, imminent Roland Garros champion Francesca Schiavone and, in the quarters, No.8 seed Samantha Stosur 6-3, 6-3.
2008 Australian Open champion Maria Sharapova was beaten in the fourth round by compatriot Dinara Safina in Paris, despite serving for the match.

Arriving in Paris as Melbourne champion for the second straight year in 2013, Azarenka recorded her best-ever result by reaching the semifinals before losing to Maria Sharapova.
2012 champion Timea Babos made a winning return to the site of her maiden title, defeating qualifier Marie Bouzkova in the first round (Abierto GNP Seguros/Rafael Velez)
